title: Senior CPU Design Verification Engineer, Devices and Services

cond_0001.intro:
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Work cross-functionally to debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 Years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Preferred Requirements
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0012.intro:
Our computational challenges are so big, complex and unique we can't just purchase off-the-shelf hardware, we've got to make it ourselves. Your team designs and builds the hardware, software and networking technologies that power all of [Company name masked]'s services. As a Hardware Engineer, you design and build the systems that are the heart of the world's largest and most powerful computing infrastructure. You develop from the lowest levels of circuit design to large system design and see those systems all the way through to high volume manufacturing. Your work has the potential to shape the machinery that goes into our cutting-edge data centers affecting millions of [Company name masked] users.
With your technical expertise, you lead projects in multiple areas of expertise (i.e., engineering domains or systems) within a data center facility, including construction and equipment installation/troubleshooting/debugging with vendors.
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.
cond_0012.responsibilities:
Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Work cross-functionally to debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0012.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around 5 years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture, or equivalent practical experience in the field.
Working knowledge of Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Background in general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Some familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture is helpful; this is an area you can continue to develop on the job.

cond_0069.intro:
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will regularly develop functional verification infrastructure and, for some roles, write diagnostic code to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams daily to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, and performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.
cond_0069.responsibilities:
Work directly with design, architecture, and performance teams to verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Actively engage cross-functionally to debug failures, clarify requirements, and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0069.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 Years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.

[Company name masked] designs and builds the hardware, software and networking technologies that power all of its services. As a Hardware Engineer, you design and build the systems that are the heart of the world's largest and most powerful computing infrastructure. Your work has the potential to shape the machinery that goes into our cutting-edge data centers affecting millions of [Company name masked] users.
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will coordinate with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to confirm architectural compliance, functional correctness, and performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.

Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design, coordinating with relevant teams as required.
Produce test plans covering verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is clear and usable.

Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.

Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.

As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of CPU verification and the systems involved.
cond_0319.responsibilities:
Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Work cross-functionally to debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0319.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 Years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.
cond_0319.values: We value excellence, achievement, and delivering outcomes we can stand behind. We aim to bring high standards and a results-focused mindset to our work.
cond_0319.workplace_support: We value work-life harmony and recognize that doing your best work should not come at the expense of life outside work. We aim to offer flexibility and support so employees can thrive both professionally and personally.

cond_0332.intro:
Our computational challenges are so big, complex and unique we can't just purchase off-the-shelf hardware, we've got to make it ourselves. The team designs and builds the hardware, software and networking technologies that power all of [Company name masked]'s services. As a Hardware Engineer, you design and build the systems that are the heart of the world's largest and most powerful computing infrastructure. You develop from the lowest levels of circuit design to large system design and see those systems all the way through to high volume manufacturing. Your work has the potential to shape the machinery that goes into our cutting-edge data centers affecting millions of [Company name masked] users.
With your technical expertise, you lead projects in multiple areas of expertise (i.e., engineering domains or systems) within a data center facility, including construction and equipment installation/troubleshooting/debugging with vendors.
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will own test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work directly with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will drive coverage analysis across various dimensions and deliver monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.
cond_0332.responsibilities:
Execute design verification using verification techniques and methodologies.
Lead cross-functional debugging of failures and take ownership of verifying the functional correctness of the design.
Develop and own test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0332.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 Years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Preferred Requirements
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.

cond_0344.intro:
Our computational challenges are so big, complex and unique we can't just purchase off-the-shelf hardware, we've got to make it ourselves. Your team designs and builds the hardware, software and networking technologies that power all of [Company name masked]'s services. As a Hardware Engineer, you design and build the systems that are the heart of the world's largest and most powerful computing infrastructure. You develop from the lowest levels of circuit design to large system design and see those systems all the way through to high volume manufacturing. Your work has the potential to shape the machinery that goes into our cutting-edge data centers affecting millions of [Company name masked] users.
With your technical expertise, you lead projects in multiple areas of expertise (i.e., engineering domains or systems) within a data center facility, including construction and equipment installation/troubleshooting/debugging with vendors.
As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance.
cond_0344.responsibilities:
Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Work cross-functionally to debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0344.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 5 years of demonstrated expertise in verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Proven track record developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Deep knowledge of Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, or Bash.
Preferred Requirements
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Advanced knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Solid understanding of ARM Instruction Set Architecture.

cond_0589.intro:
Our computational challenges are so big, complex and unique we can't just purchase off-the-shelf hardware, we've got to make it ourselves. As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will own functional verification for part of a CPU design. You will develop functional verification infrastructure and for some roles write diagnostic codes to ensure functional correctness of a design.
In this role, you will develop test plans for functional units and subsystems. You will work closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to ensure architectural compliance, functional correctness, as well as meeting performance goals. You will analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for better quality assurance. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of CPU verification and the systems involved.
cond_0589.responsibilities:
Verify designs using verification techniques and methodologies.
Work cross-functionally to debug failures and verify the functional correctness of the design.
Provide test plans, including verification strategy, environment, components, stimulus, checks, and coverage, and ensure documentation is easy to use.
cond_0589.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 Years of experience with verification methodologies and languages such as UVM and SystemVerilog.
Experience developing and maintaining verification testbenches, test cases, and test environments.
Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
Experience with Universal Verification Methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.
